the day of little businessit is often argued that the development of large businesses especially in retail fields has tended to destroy little businesses and to make it next to impossible for a man without vast capital to set up his own establishment this argument has a strong appeal but apparent facts contradict it during the depression thousands of little businesses sprung up in this country largely because of the difficulties of individuals in finding employment these little businesses offered specialized services or lower prices or were the outgrowth of a new idea of some kind many of them found a ready welcome and have prospered with the return of better times they are going ahead and in due course a percentage of them will become big businesses some of these little businesses failed because they provided poor service or did not fill a definite need but many a large business has failed for the same reasons one has only to look around any growing community today and see a legion of opportunities in retail lines for young men and women who are willing to work and realize that riches can t be earned overnight even as changing times made necessary big business combinations to serve the public so the evolutionary process has created a hundred opportunities for small retail businesses where one existed a generation ago the day of little business isn t done it is just beginning

taught economics and political science at toledo university and at antioch college it costs too much hardly a day goes by without our seeing something we want to purchase but don t because it costs merchant the merchant may be at fault in some cases but not in the majority he sells as cheaply as he possibly can knowing better than you do that high prices do more than anything else to build up sales resistance believe it or not legislation in many instances is more directly responsible for high prices than the people who make handle and sell commodities a large number of states for example have passed so called fair trade laws these laws vary in detail but all are about the same in principle they effectively block honest competition by preventing merchants from selling certain articles below a specified minimum as a result they place a premium on waste and inefficiency the high cost dealer is allowed to be the arbiter of price and value and the low cost store isn t allowed to cut the price even though it wants to and could do so and still make a satisfactory profit various local surveys concerning the econamic effects of these laws have been made and in every instance the survey have shown that they raise the cost of living and reduce sales the average family spends about all it receives in income and when prices are forced up it must buy fewer or inferior articles so don t blame your merchant when you think prices are too high most of the time he like the consumer is a victim of priceboosting policies which are beyond his control

economic freedom by oliver t beaumont in american federationistwhat is freedom it is the possession and exercise of our god given rights the undisturbed enjoyment of them whether natural civic or political it is life under a government of love rather than of force the people being themselves or by their representatives the law making power it is not permission to do as we please it is not licentiousness it is not a right or a reason for doing wrong it does not imply insubordination to authority but it is permission to do as we ought to do right to be law abiding if free we are god fearing man lov ing freedom is not the permission to do so and be so but it implies that being so and doing thus is the rule not the exception liberty for men to do as they pleased unrestrained and irresponsible would be like the ancient saturnalia short lived it would be anarchial and anarchy is but a growing youth soon ripening into the vigorous manhood of despotismwhen liberty and especially american liberty is referred to we mean the theoretic enunciation and for at least a portion of the american people the actual possession and enjoyment of human rights god given rights rights are not human gifts they are not accepted as a boon from man they are of god s creation and bestowment we thank no man for them if unjustly deprived of them and they through human intervention are restored to us we then will thank hint who has aided us to recover them from the possession of tire robber but god alone is to be praised for the gift this then is liberty the undisturbed possession and enjoyment of god given rights the opening sentence of the declaration of american independence says we hold these truths to be self evident that all men are created equal that they are endowed by their creator with certain inalienable 1 rights among which are life liberty and the pursuit of happiness the equality here announced is an 1 equality of rights not mental moral or physical equality not equality in the possession of privileges patronj age or position in all these there is heaven wide inequality but in god s sight as his creatures all have rights and though they may be robbed of them through decisions of courts the right yet remains though its exercise be forbidden here is the thrust direct at the great lie implied in hereditary or predatory wealth by which monopolies are built up and the bible contradicted when it says that god has made of one blood all men to dwell upon the face of the earth and this great truth of human equality remains and will remain however much the wicked practices of men may run counter to it and the american people be guilty of inconsistency in their glorious proclamation and their inglorious enslavement of the millions who through labor produce the wealth of the nation the right to live and let live no j man or set of men dispute and the opposite none should attempt to monopolize it is the essence of tyranny to monopolize the blessings vouchsafed to man when men do not enjoy them they are not free society owes it to all its members to protect them in the undisturbed enjoyment of life liberty equality and security of person and property except for crime committed no government through its judicial officers should interfere the penalty of the law may deprive men of their liberty degrade them from equality take away from them property or i life but while innocent and all men are considered so until proved other wise no man should be deprived of these without his consent or by trial by an impartial jury we glory as a nation in thus being j free we call no man master our i position is after having asserted the equality of men that government is established for the good of the governed not certain classes but the whole and that government derives j just powers from the consent of the i governed and that whenever any form of government fails to secure life liberty and the pursuit of happij ness it is the right of the people to alter or abolish it and institute one i that will secure these ends there is thus retained in the hands of the peopie the power of correcting abuses being themselves the sovereigns and choosing from time to time their leg islators and executive officers our motto as americans should be opinion may be left free if reason is left free to combat it our constitutional provision that congress shall make no law abridging the freedom of speech and of the press or of the rights of the people peaceably to assemble and to petition the government for a redress of grievances should be one of our greatest safeguards such in theory at least is american freedom and if we are told that practically in reference to the great army of wealth producers it is abrogated or denied we admit the charge and blush and for glaring inconsistency we tremble as we think that god is just for he has no attributes that will permit him to take sides with the oppressor against the oppressed here is our chief deficiency here is a vulnerable point which labor should fight for to see that every man has the privilege of casting his ballot and that ballot recorded as cast then that every elected official shall perform his duty to all the people many are the fears of the friends of freedom many are the predictions of the foes of free institutions let us not be blind to dangers nor refrain from looking at those things that suggest danger have we nothing to fear from the disposition of our people to act in masses swayed controlled by political leaders which they too often blindly follow have we nothing to fear from the ambition of men seeking public office that spirit of diotrephes who loved to have the pre eminence there arc patriots and patriotism is not a mere name but all are not patriots who pretend to be so before aye even after they are elected to office there arc those who would sell their country s birthright for a mess of pottage there are multitudes who have their price and like arnold would betray the lust for office and power engenders many a corrupt bargain and leads to many a condition in which liberty suffers and her children bleed we would have nothing to fear from those who exclaim o that i were made a judge in the land that every man who hath any suit or cause might come unto me and i would do him justice we have everything to fear from the decisions and acts of men high in official stations who are indifferent to the interests of the people is not ignorance and indifference and a disregard of the rights of the people when exhibited by them more fatal in its influence than when seen in men in less conspicuous positions their position gives them power their official pre eminence makes their example prevail have we nothing to fear from the internal feuds and the agitation of questions that seem to conflict with the pecuniary interests of men as between capital and the workers and which threaten a dissolution of amicable relations between the two unless justice is done have we nothing to fear from foreign immigration we will do the emigrant no injustice many of them are friends of liberty hard working and a valuable accession to us but there are others who are cast out by the foreign authorities paupers and criminals sent here in order that their governments may be delivered from the burden of providing for them every fifth man among us is a foreigner by birth we would not completely stay the tide that is setting upon us but educated as the great mass of these are under institutions so different from our own have we nothing to fear if they are left to the designs of artful politicians only a few years ago a man of foreign rank and title in speaking of america said the government of the united states ought not to stand and it will not stand but it will be destroyed by subversion and not by conquest the plan is this to send over the surplus population of europe they will go over with foreign feelings and will form a heterogeneous mass and in the course of time will be prepared to rise and subvert the government such was his language and being thus forewarned shall we fail to be fully arrfied what is the remedy we find it in economic liberty and civil liberty they must exert their united influence in the training of freedom s sons and daughters this indeed is freedom he who is imbued with the spirit of liberty will be law abiding not despising government i et the spirit of justice prevail and men will learn to respect one another that vaulting ambition which now threatens so much evil will be restrained the bad example of men in high places will give place to the manifestation of things lovely and of good report prosperity will afford means of doing good instead of luxurious indulgences and enervating pleasures when this spirit predominates then the dangers that threaten our free institutions will vanish like the mist of the morning industrial slavery will no more like the blood of abel cry aloud democracy or dictatorship for laboras the months have passed the real issue that has split the labor movement of this country has become increasingly obvious to all it is between a labor movement self governed with constitutional procedures and a movement created and controlled by an individual between the ways of a democracy and the ways of a dictator the secession movement had its origin in defiance of the constitutional authorities of the existing organization in order to put into effect policies formed by a minority in the ameripan f ederation of labor the pages of history show that causes start with minorities and win adherents on their merits but thi gt rebel group was not willing to win on its merits but decided to tear down the home that had sheltered it and on its ruins erect a bigger and better structure but human institutions are not like material structures they grow together and gain tensile strength from joint idealism collective endeavor and the common will that comes from living and working together our american federation of labor is not perfect for it consists of human beings but it has within it the capacity for development every labor movement has its periods of rapid and slow progress and essential of rapid progress is unity within the ranks of labor there were those within the american federation of labor who said let s build on what we have adding to what we have instead of scrapping years of experience and so we have done finding ways to conserve the crafts so essential to a machine era of production and to organize the workers of machine production and to co ordinate the interests of both groups for collective bargaining the american federation of labor is not all wise or perfect but it has made sincere efforts to bridge the chasm between the american f ederation of labor and the secession groups an agreement was worked out satisfactory to the representatives of that group only to be arbitrarily scrapped by the dictator of the group more recently at the request of the president of the united states peace conferences were initiated they were suspended because of the coal conferences in progress when the coal companies reached an impasse the president of the linked states intervened effectively to the end that the miners gained a complete victory then the president of the united mine workers who is also dictator of the rebel movement instead of manifesting his appreciation of the president s aid which turned defeat into victory declared that there would be no further participation in peace conferences despite his dee obligation for help despite the fact that the president s program relies upon labor support despite the repressive labor legislation passed in many states last winter and determined assaults upon state labor departments and proposals to take functions from the department of labor this dictator declared his unwillingness to bargain collectively upon matters affecting him and thereby sealed the fate of many progressive undertakings and laws no lasting labor movement can be built upon dictatorial policies and principles the welfare of groups and individuals must not be imperiled by the arbitrary decisions or the personal interests of a dictator the american labor movement will steadily move toward democratic principles and procedures and will not tolerate dictatorship within its own superior court ruling upholds prevailing wage santa clara jurist decides suit by ochs against bond firmthe california state prevailing wage law was upheld in a decision of judge coolidge sitting pro tern in the santa clara county superior court who ruled in behalf of the plaintiff in the suit of a general contractor against the bondsmen for one of his sub con tractors the decision resulted from an action arising out of the reconstruction of the santa clara courthouse and was brought by ochs general contractor for the project against the detroit fidelity under the ruling it is mandatory for contractors engaged in public work to pay the wage scale for workmen established by the state boards of supervisors or city councils regardless of the fact that workmen may be secured for lower wages after being awarded the courthouse contract ochs sub let the lathing and plastering contract to gould the sub contract providing that the prevailing wage scale be paid however according to the opinion the state division of labor statistics and law enforcement ascertained that gould was not paying lathers and plasterers the set scale and the division ordered gould or ochs to pay workmen a difference of $2466 which they should have received under the scale gould was unable to pay the amount the decision further sets forth and ochs paid in turn filing suit against the surety company which bonded gould for faithful compliance of the sub contract the surety company contended in its defense that the contractor was privileged to secure workmen at a rate lower than the wage scale and that by working the workmen evidenced their willingness to accept lower wage than that provided in the scale

recalled to the youth of america is the real spirit and background of this memorial said the officers of the association in making their announcement at the association offices at 1 east 57th street standard regardless of how any toilers may happen to be employed he is a man though the american federation of labor does not advocate strikes yet it encourages them when all other means to obtain facing the facts with philip pearlphiladelphia arriving here a couple of days before the spring 1 meeting of the of l executive council we decided to take a look at the current conference of the international labor organization where representatives of some forty one nations are trying to work out codes for the economic and social betterment of the common people of all the world in the postwar period so the next morning we got up bright and early and rode out to temple university where the sessions are being held one would have supposed that meeting here in the city of brotherly love and inspired by the highly idealistic nature of their endeavors the delegates to the ilo would constitute one happy family we were quickly disabused of such notions newspapermen delegates and hangers on of all sorts were talking only of disputes and disagreements and disaffections friction of all kinds has developed but perhaps the sharpest controversy has been precipitated by the attempts of the mexican labor leader toledano to impose the communist party line upon the ilo soviet russia is not represented at this conference having boycotted the ilo as a bankrupt organization but toledano and his group of adherents haven t let that stop them from playing the communist game here for all they are worthoasis in the jungle the surest way for the ilo to defeat its own ends is by biting off more than it can chew and digest i hat is the communist strategy and it appears so alluring that a number of liberals have been hoodwinked by it basicly and historically the ilo operates primarily in the economic field but an attempt is being made here to divert its operations info political and social areas where it has no direct jurisdiction and cannot function effectively from some of the broad proposals submitted here an outsider would gain the impression that the ilo is trying to substitute itself for the peace conference that will take place when the war ends indeed these proposals attempt to do all the work of the peace conference in advance and to make the decisions upon which even the heads of the united nations have thus far refrained from passing final judgment in this wild jungle of scattered ideas many of them highly praiseworthy others highly chimerical the clear concise opening statement of robert j watt american workers delegate stands out like a civilized oasis of common sense to quote but three paragraphs 1 believe the ilo has grown in the respect of nations because it has concentrated on its own job and has not overreached itself it is our job our scientific job to remove the causes of economic injustice it is up to us to remove the cruelty of exploitation it is up to us to help create opportunity for men to live and work as self respecting individuals but we cannot create these opportunities by resolutions here in this conference it will all work out we must concentrate our efforts in enlisting and guiding others to do this work within every nation within every community and within every industry much interest therefore is evidenced in what the ilo is gping to decide about its future role in international affairs indeed this has become the dominating issue of the conference another hot situation is developing out of the attempts of the toledano faction to oust the labor delegates from argentina because that country has a fascist government this move is opposed by the labor movements of this country great britain australia and south africa representing the great majority of organized workers in the world because other countries represented here especially south american nations are not entirely free of the fascist taint and to exclude one while admitting others would be neither just nor sensible strangely enough the discords and disagreements are not noticeable in the plenary sessions of the conference which are formal in character and slowed up by the necessity of translating each report and each motion into three different languages but the committee sessions and the lobby gossip are given over to a great deal of pulling and hauling and the rumor factory operates full blast day and night maybe we are overly optimistic but we feel that most of the controversies will be ironed out before the conference ends and a sincere practical and progressive program for the advancement of world wide economic and social democracy will be successfully formulated by the ilo

agents in securing statements and the cooperation of contractors to prove that the adopted scales were in fact the highest general prevailing wage scales in san francisco he protested against the action of a so called representative of labor not affiliated with the building trades council misrepresenting his craft and injuring to the extent of being responsible for causing wage cuts in his own at the very time that the representatives of these building trades crafts were helping his craft by having the supervisors officially recognize a higher wage than this misrepresentative of labor had agreed that his members would work for general president macdonald stated that in spite of this misrepresentative s statement to the supervisors that he was not interested in what scale of wages the supervisors set and of his persistent endeavor to drag down the scales of the basic crafts that he macdonald assisted by the representatives of the basic crafts had secured the adoption of an $8 scale green s splendid labor day address to the nationwilliam green president of the american federation of labor delivered the following address at the labor day celebration in canton ohio september 2 1935 over a national hook up of the national broadcasting company in transmitting this labor day message i feel justified in sounding a note of optimism and hopeful encouragement there is abundant evidence at hand which shows that the nation is gradually emerging from a long continued period of distressing and painful economic experiences we look hack upon six years of unemployment impaired human values financial collapse and mounting losses during which the size of an army of idle men and women fluctuated between ten and thirteen million those were painful days for labor for working men and women were the chief victims of econojnic demoralization words cannot adequately describe the mental and physical suffering through which they passed those days of darkness and discouragement were both oppressive and depressive only brave courageous men and women can pass through such an ordeal and at the same time maintain their faith in the existing sociaj order but through all the sad experiences met during the long period which has intervened since the financial and economic collapse of 1929 labor maintained self control and demonstrated its unswerving loyalty and devotion to the nation s institutions its hope and confidence in the resourcefulness of the nation and its faith in the fundamental principles of democracy were subjected to a most severe test every act of self discipline courage service and constructive endeavor revealed the soundness of uie foundation upon which the movment of our country rests now the economic horizon is becoming brighter we can enter into the spirit of labor day this year firm in the belief that better days are at hand that even though slowly yet surely we are moving toward the realization of a better economic and social order increasing and enlarging work opportunities and improved conditions of employment ihe basis för this better social and economic order has been laid hictitious values are being liquidated speculation is being ended and the nation is becoming social minded all of this is reflected in the advanced and progressive position which the legislative bodies of the nation have assumed in the consideration and enactment of security and s ci al justice legislation the nvnri rlj the nation comprehends more fully now than ever before the social obligation of industry and the owners of industry a sordid materialistic point of view such as prevailed during the reckless social and speculative days of 1929 is being supplanted by a humane social and more spiritual attitude it is my opinion however that in this respect we are just in the formative period of a social justice program and policy which will ultimately be expanded so as to provide for adequate and proper care for those who are unemployed the aged who are dependent the sick who are dependent and who need medical care and attention and the under fed and under nourished children ofj the nation who must ever be the objects of special care and consideration a mere appraisement of all these possibilities must add to the significance of this year s celebration of labor s national holiday since we celebrated labor day last year events have occurred whjch have been of tremendous importance to labor this year can properly be designated as one of unusual social and economic experi mentation labor has taken an active part in all that has taken place and has been effected either favorably or unfavorably by all the changes which have taken place when the supreme court held the national recovery act invalid section 7a which conferred upon labor the right to organize and bargain collectively free from coercion and intimidation on the part of employers and which was incorporated in all industrial codes of fair competition was nullified and set aside code making and code observance terminated and in manv instances industry returned to the pursuit of practices which were detrimental to the economic and industrial welfare of the men and women employed in industry i he american federation of labor appreciating fully the importance and significance of the supreme court s decision acted quicklj supported a bill sponsored by senator o mahoney which provides for the licensing of corporations this act if passed by congress will provide for industrial stabilization constructive economic planning and the establishment and maintenance of fair industrial and labor practices labor will call upon the congress of the lnited states to enact this measure into law when it convenes next january1 he termination of the national recovery act very seriously affected decent employers of labor who sought to maintain code standards and labor which was fighting vigorously for the establishment of decent wages and decent conditions of employment it is always the ruthless irresponsible employer who through the pursuit of a policy of exploitation tears down wage structures disregards fcjrtr de practices and destroys decent conditions of employment rule this class of employers is in the minority the volume of manufactured goods and commodities which they produce is a factor in maiket condition through the imposition of unwarranted lowered wage and working standards upon their employes they are able to under sell the fair employers this in turn tends to break down the wage structure erected by labor through years of effort and striursrle herefore the question which the people through their government must meet and answer is whether a form of economic planning shall be adopted and applied which will require all employers to comply with fair minimum standards or whether we shall continue the pursuit ot a policy of destructive competition merely because it is alleged that individual ownership of manufacturing industries carries with it the right to do as they please e are able to appraise the destructive effects of such a policy since the decision of the supreme court which held the national ecovery act invalid reports from all sections of the nation received at the offices of the american federation of labor while incomplete show that code standards have broken down in more than twenty thousand manufacturing wholesale retail and service industrial units reductions cif rates of pay and an increase in hours of work nave adversely affected more than five million workers these are facts which cannot be controverted they show the extent to which some employers wdl go when freed from restraint such as was impose iroug i the code making process naturally the unorganized unprotected workers suffered the most but all workers have been injured through the breakdown which followed the collapse of the national recovery act the experience through which labor passed and the lessons it learned during the period of economic experimentation are proving to be of very great value working people everywhere are understanding as never before the potential as well as the actual power strength and influence of organization and collective bargaining they know that the mobilization of the economic strength of yorkers in all lines of industry is necessary in order to protect them against j exploitation and to sustain them in any aggressive effort they may intake to secure and enjoy higher standards of life and living no code making policy however meritorious and helpful it mav be can serve as a substitute for collective bargaining carried on and supported by a solid united militant organization of working men and women  has made gains because it learned to place a true value upon nation within the next few years employers of labor should accept this situation they cannot prevent the workers from organizing through the pursuit of a policy of discharge persecution and fixed national policy should be supported and upheld by all classes of people including employ ers of labor  1 he progress which labor has made both in the pursuit of its onomic and legislative policies is definite and most substantial ihe two policies run parallel we seek to promote the common cause of labor through the utilization of the economic influence and power of labor and advance the cause of social justice and legal protection through the enactment of state and federal legislation labor has ever held as it now holds that it must be free to bargain collectively for wages hours by clarkethe untimely death of melvin a traylor president of one of chicago s largest banks who rose from a childhood in a log cabin on a kentucky hillside removes from american finance one of its most picturesque and independently minded figures he was the oldest of seven children traylor was outspoken he hit with a punch and expressed himself in pithy sentences and keen edged thoughts that indicated neither fear or favor lie had a pleasant and engaging personality but an individuality that kept him rooted to precepts learned in the hard days of childhood and as a struggling bank clerk in texas traylor might easily have been a banker of orthodox conservatism for he followed in the footsteps and assumed the task of the late james a forgan as president of chicago s first national bank forgan ruled with an austere hand in days when ruthless individualism was the heart and soul of american business and industry helped unpaid teachers but traylor was of different material beneath his calm exterior of banker there was a warm glow of human understanding w hen chicago school teachers pavless for months and in destitution appealed to him to assist them in obtaining back salaries he remembered the days when he was a school teacher on leatherwood creek in the kentucky mountains and called in the bankers and arranged for acceptance of more of chicago s doubtful and depreciated tax anticipation warrants so the teachers would have money naturally conservative in his financial thought he nevertheless struck out with a ferocity that amazed his hearers at the speculative practices and stock market methods of the hey dey prior to 1929 when speaking before the international chamber of commerce in washington in 1931 he said then i urge consideration of the complete abolishment of so called floor trading which as i am informed has about it most of the characteristics of plain crapshooting and few if any more redeeming features of that delightful ethiopian pastime speech is scathing indictment it was a ringing speech a speech of savage attack and denunciation of practices and methods which he said had plunged the nation into depression and brought about the condition that was plunging the country into one of its direct calamities bankers and industrialists sat in dismay and amazement as they listened to his strictures a scathing and terriffic indictment which was later borne out and vindicated in the startling disclosures of the senate committee on banking and currency coming to a climax in the testimony of wiggin dillon and morgan and still in progress the air around the united states chamber of commerce was frigid for traylor after that speech those who had scowled as his booming voice intoned its indictment of high finance as practiced in high places turned a shoulder in his direction afterward previously he had been active in chamber affairs and on chamber committees but he did not again figure in any of its affairs of modern school report was that president roosevelt wanted traylor for either his director of the budget or comptroller of currency but he resisted the call to remain in his chosen field as a banker he was distinctly of the modern school of banker and keenly alive to the problems and difficulties that beset the banking conditions of the country

the new plan of securing a homemr editor this part of the salinas valley is all stirred up over a matter that i think would furnish some interesting reading for many of your subscribers about two months ago it was quietly announced down here that the arroyo seco ranch 000 acre tract of land lying between soledad and king city on the west side of the salinas river had been sold the first announcement made no particular impression as it was not known by the people here that there was any special change to be made in the use of the land in a very short time however it became known that almost the entire tract had already been disposed of to home seekers who were to commence coming on to the land just as soon as the title could be passed to them four thousand acres of the land is under a very fine system of irrigation and this part of the ranch has been taken in small tracts ranging from 2 to 20 acres the remainder of the ranch has been taken in tracts ranging from 10 to 100 acres the irrigation system belongs to these people and the part of the land that is now without water can easilly be supplied and the water they own is sufficient when properly developed for much more than the entire tract inquiry shows that there are many peculiar features to the plan by which this settlement of the people is being accomplished for instance the home seeker gets his land at just the price per acre that the company the california home extension association paid for it in a body plus an allotment fee of $lo each which it appears is all the company gets out of it this gives the home seeker his land at about one third of what he could have purchased a single small tract of such irrigated land for not only do these home seekers get their land at these low figures but they also count on a sudden and very great increase in the market value of their land as a result of such a large number of people coming on to the land almost at once again the association seems to understand that the land will have this great increase in value underthese circumstances and knowing that they are thus well secured they make payment s very easy where it is desired a town called clark city named after the author of this new method of handling land has been laid out in the midst of the tract it consists of about 1000 residence and business lots most of which are 50x150 feet and it is said that more than half of them are already sold these also are sold at cost plus the small allotment fee now i think your readers can see that this is something new under the sun and from the smiling faces of these newcomers one would think they were well satisfied with the way this new thing works the steamers touching at monterey bay and the trains from both north and south are bringing in these people to their new homes every day and clark city that is to be is the liveliest place in all this section it is said by these people that about all lines of business will be represented in this young city by the coming fall including a first national bank large amounts of live stock farming implements and household goods are being hauled to this new town from all the nearby railroad stations clark city for the present consists mainly of a large number of tents but the fifty or seventy five ablebodied workers that are there now with the many more that are reported to be on the way will change things very rapidly the association mentioned above has offices in the james mood building san francisco and in the chamber of commerce los angeles i hope their work may prove to be good and permanent subscriber

the american invasion of north africa and the allied offensive in libya as the forerunner of a second front in europe addressing a mess meeting of 20 000 in madison square garden new york city mr green declared surely the momentum of the new offensive cannot and will not be permitted to end with the defeat of the axis armies on only one sector of the world s battlefronts i prefer to accept it as a battle just begun we do not know nor can we safely anticipate where or in what way this allied offensive will be extended and carried forward we must leave that to the military experts of the united nations who are planning their strategy on a world wide basis mr green who spoke at a meeting arranged by the congress of american soviet friendship also gave high praise to the stalwart defense of the russian armies on the eastern front he said hitler s day is done the heroic russian army has stopped him in his tracks for many long weeks the nazi forces have thrown all their military resources against stalingrad only to be checked and beaten back day after day by russia s gallant defenders stalingrad has become the verdun of this war its brave defenders have blocked hitler s government is discharging its obligation to our russian allies labor demands that aid to russia be real and vital not merely an unfulfilled promise secondly labor on its own part must become thoroughly conscious of its responsibilities and reach new heights of production it must firmly resolve that there shall not be a moment s interruption in war production for any cause for the duration scale allied offensive that is why military strategy and sound common sense both dictate the continuation and expansion of the new drive so auspiciously launched in north africa

challenge wage cutsas delay in the upswing in business continues the hazards for labor standards increase industries are everywhere looking for sources of revenues to maintain dividends wage earners should be on guard to protect their incomes against further invasions further reductions in wage rates at the present time would be most unfortunate and would tend to offset the efforts of the government to create better business conditions congress has enacted legislation to make credit available for banks and industries and to provide for f ederal reserve banks secondary reserves for issuing reserve notes as a result the credit contraction policies have relaxed bond prices have risen stock prices have developed strength price decline is less rapid some companies are beginning to write down stock values on their books thus eliminating inflated values when business sets its house in order the maintenance of buying power is of growing importance unless consumers are financed to buy the output of industries the warehouses and retail shelves are soon overstocked wage earners and small salaried persons constitute 80 per cent of retail customers they have a responsibility to help maintain buying power by keeping their own incomes stable wage earners must be a self directing agency if they are to help to maintain the balance for prosperity it is their industrial and public duty to challenge all wage cuts proposals wage earners not only have a right to a voice in determining their share of the return on the products they helped produce but they have a right to know for what purpose any reductions in their wages are to be used wage earners have a right to know how the directors have disposed of the resources of the industry they have a right to propose other economies as substitutes for pay cuts effective and insistent use of facts for their own protection is the first defense against wage cuts

give us more freedom and less unemployment we demand modification of the volstead act or repealwashington in convention has reaffirmed its position and our fight will continue said matthew woll president and 1 m ornburn secretary treasurer of labor s national committee for modification of the volstead act on their return from the american federation of labor convention where they received fresh authority and instructions to continue the campaign for modification we have said the issue no longer is whether there is to be modification american public sentiment has become so aroused that modification at least is certain the real issue is whether we shall stop at modification or whether an outraged and aroused people may not sweep away the whole prohibition structure stands for modification our fight is for modification we believe every purpose will be served by modification modification is our goal if modification proves less than we hope and believe it will prove we reserve the right to change our goal believes in taking today s step today dry autocracy opposed finally american labor believes that the american people have a right to have what they desire and that they have a right to the opportunity to say what they desire the so called prohibitionists would fasten upon us an autocracy in which they would dictate to us what we shall have and when we shall have opportunity to exercise a voice in determining issues we oppose autocracy we believe we have a right to continuous and effective voice and if in exercising that voice we make a mistake we have the unquestioned right to make that mistake but it is not we who are heading toward the making of a mistake the mistake has been made the most tragic mistake in our national history the mistake was made when under the cover of an abnormal situation this sad and miserable fiasco was foisted upon a people who had no chance to speak either in approval or disapproval we came out of a war for democracy to fall victim to autocracy in its most hideous form at home well we are resolved to remedy the wrong to unseat the usurpers to be free again liquor only one issue in earlier years our people were disturbed because their right to partake of the beverages of their choice had been stolen from them at first their resentment was directed against that single thing today the issue has grown infinitely larger and the question of the right to partake of alcoholic beverages is only one of many questions involved in the prohibition issue the whole attitude of our people toward law is changing and since constituted government expresses itself in law the meaning of the situation is that the attitude of our people toward government itself is changing no republic can well afford to allow a condition in which the people resent government our safety lies in affection for government and unstinted support of government this we can have only when the people feel that the government is theirs responding to their will so far as i am aware there is no nation that has adopted and continued to maintain prohibition where the people have had the chance to vote on the issue regulation there has been but there has not been absolute prohibition maintained in effect by the people after experience the people know what the reformers do not know or will not learn they know that prohibition is impossible they know it is unwise to attempt it and that it is wholly unsound as a doctrine temperance is goal we stand for modification for many reasons prohibition is wrong in principle prohibition debases society and government modification means a return to sanity to cleanliness and to temperance temperance was the original and proper goal of those in america who fought the liquor traffic of old modification means a tremendous stimulus to employment thousands will return to work and the economic gain will be enormous perhaps equal to the actual gain in volume of employment important as that is at this juncture would be the gain in confidence in mental balance and relief on the part of a people who could again face the future conscious that a great wrong had been righted modification means a burst of energy throughout the whole commercial world the propaganda calculated to induce us to think modification would take money from other industries is of a piece with all of the hoodwinking propaganda we have had from the sanctuaries and burrows of the professional prohibitionists there is not the slightest scintilla of evidence to that effect our organization proposes to take this issue before the coming session of congress and the doleful predictions of the professionals to the contrary notwithstanding we expect to win america cannot afford to postpone this issue there are some things that cannot be put off except at a risk and cost too great we are paying in crime in racketeering in gangsterism in debased morality and poisoned citizenship altogether too much for this experiment which never has been noble either in purpose or in effect i am authorized to say to you that the american labor movement is in this fight to win not for itself but for our nation and our people labor has not always had so many allies p nd supporters in its struggles for human freedom and justice perhaps not in all things is the average man among us so personally and vitally interested perhaps not in all things are right and wrong so obvious but here all can see the way all are interested none can escape the issue or its consequences it is in the broadest sense of the word a popular issue by which i mean a people s issue the early zealots of temperance have pretty well passed from the picture as participants in the so called prohibition movement today that movement is a movement of professional propagandists professional organizers and politicians those who once sought temperance through prohibition must now seek temperance through an undoing of the work of fanatics temperance is not found in denial the word means just what it appears to mean america given the chance will always be a temperance nation america will always re erit autocracy and it will always rebel against decrees and impositions god help our nation when it humbly bows the knee to tyrants of whatever kind they may be finally our nation born to lead toward freedom will always find its course toward that noble goal and i give you the word of labor that our hosts will go marching on to the day of victory ours is no distant objective the issue is critical victory must not be long delayed

standard of living for the workers in reply to questions from the floor at the end of his hour long address mr woll defended labor s attitude saying it often had extended offers of cooperation which could be if its cooperation was accepted the greatest factor in the preservation of private enterprise if labor and capital cooperate he continued the power of government will not be used to destroy us if not god knows what will happen to our social order in his prepared speech mr woll asserted that the time had come when government must encourage business and industry by every means possible to create new wealth and employment and when denunciation of private enterprise must cease jhe speaker proposed incentive taxation to encourage plant expansion and payment of higher wages by a system of tax deductions to apply when certain provisions are complied with i he possibilities of incentive taxation are new and important he continued 1 lie subject should be given careful study by both the found fortune s start in subway gold mine one day ten years ago said a western millionaire to a chicago herald examiner writer i stood without a nickel and without the door of a restaurant in san francisco i was indulging in an optical feast gazing at the display of uncooked roasts chops and steaks garnished with watercress and altogether lovely in the window the song or rather its refrain thou art so near and yet so far was whispered to me by the gaunt brownie of hunger then a prosperous looking man who was flipping a half dollar in his hand dropped the coin which tinkled through an iron grate and fell into a subway below the man gave an almost unconcerned glance in the direction the coin had gone and then went away humming a popular air i always possessed some resource and i was determined to possess that coin the occasion is what is frequently spoken of as a ground hog case i was out of meat also bread i spoke to the proprietor of the place told him i had dropped a $5 gold piece through the grate and asked if i might go and retrieve it certainly he said and gave me a hatchet with which i might remove a wooden bar that had been nailed across a door leading to the basement to the opening under the grate there was much litter and dust down there and in searching for the lost coin i found many others which had been dropped in a similar way thus i cleaned up $8 from that prospect drift the amount supplied me with a place to put the able bodied appetite which i hqd concealed about my person it also gave me an entree to a clean shirt and a proportionate supply of self esteem and selfreliance 9 i visited men of influence whom i had not been sufficiently courageous to meet in the immediate heretofore and i have not been seriously insolvent since that day thus you may see on what a slender thread oft hangs a chance in life the practical trade unionist always demands the union label shop card or button

by bus rep carl sundahlfull employment or unemployment i am assuming there will be other accounts in this paper written of the conference on full employment held last saturday at san francisco state college the 450 500 people present ranged from famous names in union circles who were present as speakers and panel members to several california assemblymen to university of california experts on industrial relations to average people like you and me all these people were there to tackle the question what to do about unemployment we can t continue to ignore the gradually rising level of unemployment more youngsters and oldsters cut off from work automation and new trade techniques continuing at increasing speeds at this conference on full employment hundreds of people asked themselves what to do about it and many came up with many answers but usually the first answer was a shorter work week and the answer to this was usually that the shorter work week only compensated for some of the increased productivity of modern industry and failed to put more people to workthe next answer was almost always earlier retirement the idea being that earlier retirement of active workers will provide more jobs for the younger people flooding the labr market however many speakers ranging from dr carstens who is head of the institute of industrial relations of the university of california at los angeles to harry bridges of the international longshoremen and warehousemen s lnion agreed that a new requirement should go with the earlier retirement cure for unemployment proposals the requirement must be that retirement must be accompanied by a decent retirement income why probably 90 per cent of the present group of people retiring from work are retiring to a long life of poverty the average working man can look forward to 20 years of life on an income about equal to unemployment benefits in addition they generally lose the fringe benefits of their trade vacation pay fair heath and welfare benefits they retire to live on onefourth to one and one third of their previous income where does the consumer demand for production go when these thousands retiring each week drop from $5oo 900 a month to $5o to $250 a month income what are some of the questions or angles to consider one raising retirement payments social security sharply will raise consumer demand sharply and have a strong effect on unemployment two provide free comprehensive medical and hospital care to all retired people results a happier and healthier group of people who will have happier relatives and a big market for new clothes apartments hospitals doctors and nurses plus the schools and gear to train them more employment for the people people at the conference agreed that the retired person in our communities should be treated by society in a civilized manner should be well fed well clothed well housed medicared without any of theamerican medical association baloney about over 65 types of insurance there are as many retired people now in california as there are working union members and the number of retired persons is increasing as technological unemployment forces us to say all people want to retire early we are simply masking growing unemployment as early retirement the economics of our national daily life require greater consumer demand to provide work for the presently employed if we don t legislate nationally to give a sharp boost to consumer demand unemployment or early retirement is going to come to younger and younger people but to make it worse these younger people will find they are eligible only for temporary unemployment benefits but are too young for the povety of early retirement being too young to qualify for social security benefits this country can make a big start on this problem there are many things to do that must be done we can tame the universe police the world store more power in bombs than all the production needed would consume we must face the fact that unemployment or the poverty of early retirement is a national problem a menace to our national collective security a creeping enemy blotting our image before the world and as such should be given the generous attention and budget that other menaces to national security receive o holidays to all

value of shorter workdaywriting of the philosophy of the shorter workday samuel gompers editor of the american federation says in part as a matter of fact the entire history of the world demonstrates clearly that the workmen whose hours of daily labor are comparatively low are those who receive not only comparatively but actually higher wages and this is true as between the workers of any of the countries on the face of the globe this is equally true as between any two states or cities in any country it is true as between any two industries in any one city and it is even true as between two different establishments in any one industry in the same vicinity wherever the hours of daily labor are longest the wages are lowest wherever the hours of daily labor are shortest the wages are highest in truth the same economic law governs even in any one given large industrial establishment in such an establishment having in view of course only the wage earners we find that those who enter it earliest in the morning and leave it latest at night receive the lowest wages paid to employes in that stablishment while those who enter it latest and leave it earliest in the afternoon or evening receive the highest wages paid to any of the employes therein this is due to economic law and is founded in the philosophy that the wage earners whose hours of daily toil are long become physically enfeebled mentally dwarfed and stunted and have few wants apart from their bare necessities of life while on the other hand the wage earners whose hours of daily labor are shortest that is an eight hour or approximately eight hour workday demand and aspire to the highest and best standard of living whose luxury of yesterday is the necessity of to day and whose constant aspiration is for the better nobler and higher life

wage policy and full employmentwhen representatives of labor say that full employment after the war must be based on a high general level of wages they are often accused of speaking in the interest of a single social group sometimes they are even told that the wages they are striving for would endanger the welfare of the working class itself for these reasons it is important to note that a number of experts on economic questions outside the labor movement endorse labor s wage policy this is shown by statements recently made by leading figures in the federal reserve board the country s central monetary authority one of these statements was made by the chairman of the board of governors of the federal reserve system mariner s eccles another by goldenweiser the board s economic advisor in the division of research and statisticsboth experts emphasize the need for a high level of consumption after the war as the basis of a full employment policy mr eccles insists that a high level of consumption will be needed primarily to insure full employment mr goldenweiser stresses the social aspects of high consumption as well and demands that there should be established a standard of living below which no person in this country need fall under any circumstances a minimum of food a minimum of clothing a minimum of shelter education and medical care and even of money that is the floor on which to start and below which no one should have to fall i think that is basic i think our minimum standard is too low and we have to find means of raising it how can we reach the high level of consumption which is required for full employment both mr eccles and mr goldenweiser think we must extend social security and establish a tax system which does not lay too great a burden on low income groups but most important of all they say is an adequate wage policy a high level of consumers expenditures is not possible without a large volume of wage and salary income mr eccles insists if our economy is to operate at full capacity average wage and salary incomes must be high enough at normal hours of work to give the people sufficient purchasing power to take the product off the market when after the war hours return to normal and overtime pay is discontinued total wage and salary income will decline sharply if we are to avoid sharply declining prices and loss of markets which discourage production and business expansion a gradual upward adjustment will be necessary in the wages and the salaries of the great mass of comparatively low paid workers this must be accomplished without increasing prices otherwise the desired increases in consumption would be absorbed by a rise in the cost of living increases in productivity should be passed on to the public largely in the form of higher wages and salaries mr goldenweiser recommends much the same postwar wage policy as mr eccles he is emphatic in demanding an upward adjustment of wages after the war in order to offset at least in part the loss of overtime payment and to correct injustices which have developed during the period of wartime controlsin order to secure a decent standard of living for low income groups one which would at the same time place a floor under consumption mr goldenweiser emphatically stresses the importance of better labor organization among the lowest income groups where we have effective organization we usually have better standards mr goldenweiser insists i think he continues that the best way in which standards can be obtained without too much government interference is by increased bargaining power and bargaining power means organization therefore what we need is better organization among the lower income groups this should be a broad objective of public policy
